title: Shakti as a philosophy
hook: earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, the sense of I: in the Gita, Krishna calls the whole list his nature, and then says there's more

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Shvetashvatara Upanishad: seekers set down their list of answers, sat, and saw God's own power hidden in its own qualities.

Earth. Water. Fire. Air. Space. Mind. Intellect. The sense of I. In the seventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna lists these one after another, the way you'd unpack a box onto a table. The ground under your feet, the thoughts in your head, even the feeling of being someone: all on one list. Then he says: this is my nature. Mine. And before Arjuna can take that in, he adds: and this is the lower one. There's another.
screen: `EARTH, WATER, FIRE, AIR, SPACE.` → `MIND, INTELLECT, THE SENSE OF I.` → `THIS IS MY NATURE. THE LOWER ONE.`

segments.voice: Here are the verses, in paraphrase. Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and the sense of I: this is my prakriti, my nature, divided eightfold. That is the lower. Know my other, higher nature, the life in things, by which this whole world is upheld. All beings come from these two, as from a womb. I am where the whole world begins, and where it dissolves. First, the word. Prakriti: nature, the stuff and the shaping of things. Krishna calls it his. Matter isn't the enemy of the divine here; it belongs to God. Second, what's on the lower list. Mind, intellect and the sense of I are there too. The thoughts you're thinking right now are, in the Gita's picture, part of nature. Third, the higher nature: the life that holds the world up. Some readers hear every living being in it; others hear the spark of awareness in each one. Either way, the world doesn't just sit there. It's held. Fourth, the week. Here the Gita speaks through Krishna; in the days ahead, a goddess text takes up this same word, prakriti, in her own voice. Look back. Parvati, tested in the forest by a visitor in disguise, and feeding Shiva in Kashi. Ramakrishna's snake, still or moving. Shiva who can't stir without Shakti. A blade of grass that fire and wind couldn't move, and Uma who named the power behind them. Seekers who saw God's own power hidden in the world. And now Krishna: all of this is mine, and there is more.
screen: `PRAKRITI: MY NATURE, EIGHTFOLD.` · `EVEN MIND AND THE SENSE OF I.` · `THE HIGHER NATURE HOLDS THE WORLD UP.` · `THE WEEK: A VERSE, A STRAW, A SEEING.` · then, large: `ALL OF THIS IS MINE, AND THERE IS MORE.`

segments.voice: Walk Krishna's list slowly, one breath each: earth, your weight on the seat; water, the wet of the mouth; fire, warm hands; air, the breath; space, the room; mind, the next thought; intellect, the part that names it; the sense of I. Then rest in whatever is aware of the whole list. If you pray, you can offer the list back in the words you use.
Shakti as a philosophy. In the Gita, earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and the sense of I make up the lower nature, and a higher one holds the world up.
Your line: Shakti as a philosophy. Even a racing mind belongs to nature. Rest well.

howItsDone: The Bhagavad Gita's seventh chapter is studied and chanted in homes and Gita classes, and teachers use its two natures, lower and higher, to explain how the divine relates to the world.

original.note: Sanskrit: prakriti, nature. In the Gita, Krishna calls his nature lower and higher.

trapdoor: what you thought: nature is rocks and rivers, and the mind is something else.
what it means: in the Gita, earth and mind and the sense of I are all one nature, the lower one, and a higher nature holds the world up.
what a scholar hears: Gita 7.4–5, bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā; apareyam, and parā, the jīvabhūtā, by which the world is held.

the Rig Veda's hymn of creation

chat.says: Krishna puts mind and thoughts on the same list as earth and water? Why?
options: In Gita 7, mind, intellect and the sense of I are his lower nature, like earth and water.
He's listing the gifts he'll hand Arjuna if Arjuna agrees to fight in the battle.
He's naming what Arjuna owns, so Arjuna knows his body and mind are his alone.
chat.meaning: Krishna names eight parts of his lower nature, prakriti, mind and the sense of I among them, and a higher nature that holds the world up.
